newsitem.title: ITALY: Rome says unaware of Italian link to Paris bomb.
newsitem.headline: Rome says unaware of Italian link to Paris bomb.

text.p: Italian Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano said on Thursday that he had no evidence to support newspaper reports that Tuesday's Paris train bombing may have been carried out by extremists who entered France from Italy.
"I don't know of any indications by the French authorities corresponding to what has been published today in some newspapers," the minister told parliament.
Two people were killed in the blast which was thought to be the work of Algerian Islamic guerrillas.

The Armed Islamic Group (GIA) claimed responsibility for a series of blasts last year that killed eight people and injured more than 160 others, accusing France of backing the military authorities in Algiers in a war against Islamists.
The Turin newspaper La Stampa carried a front page headline on Thursday: "Paris, the killers came from Italy."
Corriere della Sera reported: "Paris, Italian trail for the bomb."
Both newspapers said French anti-terrorism agents had been warned in November that an "eight-man commando" of bombers was about to arrive in France from Italy.
Napolitano, answering a parliamentary question, said that the chief of French and Italian police had met in Paris on Monday and he was unaware of any particular apprehension.
"We have close links with the interior ministry and the French police. We maintain such contacts with mutual satisfaction. In Italy we are on maximum alert," he said.
Napolitano cited arrests of Algerians in some Italian cities last month on suspicion of involvement in terrorist activities and organisations.
Italian police said on November 7 that they had arrested 22 people on suspicion of supplying arms, false documents and other support to the GIA.

Investigators in the northwest city of Turin, from where the operation was spearheaded after a year of surveillance, said at the time that they believed the suspects may have supplied logistical support for bomb attacks last year in France.
Several suspected GIA supporters were arrested in Italy last year in a similar operation to November's.
